description.narrative:
Insatsen berör stöd till Urgent Action Sister Funds program ”Sustaining feminist activism worldwide” och täcker perioden Januari 2024 till December 2028 och en total budget om 175 000 000 SEK.
Urgent Action Sister Funds är ett konsortium av fyra fonder som verkar för att skydda kvinnliga, trans och icke-binära människorättsförsvarare och för att främja deras verksamhet. Fonderna förmedlar två typer av snabba och flexibla stöd till människorättsförsvarare, dels säkerhetstöd (security grants) till människorättsförsvarare vars säkerhet och trygghet är i omedelbar fara och dels det de kallar ”opportunity grants” vilket är snabba stöd för brådskande och tidsavgörande påverkansinsatser. Det övergripande målet för verksamheten är att stödja och främja kvinnliga, trans och ickebinära människorättsförsvarare och deras sociala rörelser som verkar för jämställdhet, demokrati och mänskliga rättigheter.
Urgent Action Sister Funds har över 25 års erfarenhet av att ge akuta skyddsstöd och har sedan den första fonden etablerades 1997 förmedlat mer än 50 miljoner USD via mer än 8300 stödbidrag. Tillsammans har de medarbetare i 33 länder och ett nära samarbete med över 700 rådgivare i 165 länder som är aktiva i rörelser för mänskliga rättigheter och social rättvisa. Fonderna ingår i ett globalt ekosystem för skydd och säkerhet för MR-försvarare och de utmärker sig som särskilt betrodda bland just kvinnliga och feministiska människorättsförsvarare.
Insatsen är relevant för strategin för ”Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete för global jämställdhet och kvinnors och flickors rättigheter 2022-2026" och i synnerhet mål 4 ”Stärka förutsättningar för kvinnorättsorganisationer att verka oberoende och långsiktigt samt öka trygghet och säkerhet för kvinnorättsförsvarare”.
Verksamheten tar avstamp i FN-konventionen om de mänskliga rättigheterna och förväntas bidra till FN's utvecklingsagenda och i synnerhet SDG 5. Insatsen är även väl i linje med EU’s handlingsplan för Jämställdhet (EU GAP III), inte minst genom dess fokus på intersektionella dimensioner av diskriminering och vikten att främja hbtqi-personers rättigheter, som betonas i EU’s handlingsplan för jämställdhet.

The contribution concerns support to The Urgent Action Sister Fund's program "Sustaining feminist activism worldwide". It covers the period January 2024 to December 2028 and a total budget of SEK 175 000 000.
Urgent Action Sister Funds is a consortium of four funds that work to protect women, trans and non-binary human rights defenders and to promote their work and movements. The funds provide two types of rapid and flexible support to human rights defenders: security grants to human rights defenders whose safety and security are at immediate risk and opportunity grants, which are rapid support for urgent and time-sensitive advocacy efforts. The overall goal of their work is to support and promote female, trans and non-binary feminist human rights defenders and their social movements.
Urgent Action Sister Funds have over 25 years of experience in providing rapid response grants and have since the first fund was established in 1997 provided more than USD 50 million through more than 8300 grants. Together, they have employees in 33 countries and work closely with over 700 advisors in 165 countries who are active in human rights and social justice movements.
The funds are part of a global ecosystem for the protection and security of human rights defenders and they stand out as particularly trusted among feminist activists around the world.

The overall aim is to protect and advance the civil, political and social rights of women and LGBTI persons and to invest in social justice movements (including environmental, feminist, anti- corruption, land rights, peace, youth and LGBTI movements).
This by contributing to the following objectives:
1) Increased and more accessible resources to meet the urgent needs of women, trans and non-binary Human Rights Defenders, their organizations and movements provided collectively by the UAFs and individually in each Funds respective regions.
2) The four Urgent Action Funds has a strong architecture that evolves as needed to enable collaboration and learning on key themes across Funds.
3) Women, trans, and non-binary Human Rights Defenders have strengthened their understanding of collective care and protection as a critical sustainability strategy for themselves and their work
4) The UAFs advocacy have promoted a more equitable sharing of resources and power in philanthropy and supports the agency of women, trans, and non-binary Human Rights Defenders to demand the transformation of power between donors and Human Rights Defenders.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
(Objective 1)
The funds have continued to map potential scenarios of attacks on their organizations and the philanthropic sector, particularly in the United States, in an effort to track rapidly changing political conditions and prioritize the safety and wellbeing of staff and grantee partners. Given that a high percentage of resourcing for the Sisterhood collective and resourcing for individual Urgent Action Funds stems from private philanthropy in the United States, what happens in the United States impacts all four Urgent Action Funds. Based on the potential scenarios, the funds are taking steps to protect the assets of the Urgent Action Funds.
Strengthening financial resilience has become increasingly important for the funds given the shifts in the global funding landscape. UAF are tracking declines in their funding that started in 2025 and will continue to impact the Urgent Action Funds and others in the feminist, civic space and human rights sectors in the coming years. The funds have proactively been pursuing humanitarian funding in collaboration with peers, engaging in the mainstream climate sector and have continued to seek new bilateral funding. In 2024 they successfully brought two more bilateral donors on board, Global Affairs Canada and Irish Aid. UAF reports that Sidas support in the relation building with Irish Aid was important.
The UAFs have further continued their work to enhance the digital safety infrastructure by engaging in work such as implementing comprehensive security audits, investing in software and hardware authentication protocols, upgrading system software proactively to prevent vulnerabilities, reviewing system access management and monitoring, and enhancing methods to push through regular security updates, enforce encryption, and maintain control over devices used to access organizational systems.
Objective 2)
In 2024, the Urgent Action Urgent Action Funds total collective grantmaking, including grants resourced via Sida, totalled 2,133 awards to women, trans and non-binary HRDs, their groups, and networks in 140 countries for a total of more than USD $20M. Almost 1,800 (85%) of grants were given to HRDs living in obstructed, repressed, or closed countries by the Civicus Monitor (25% from total grants given were in the last category, the highest percentage to closed countries since we started to track this indicator).
Across regions, the Urgent Action Funds continue to support grantee partners working in contexts of conflict, growing repression and militarization, climate crises, displacement, and criminalization of civil society movements and HRDs. The growing threats and violence defenders and their organizations are experiencing were reflected in the high volume of requests for protection, security and wellbeing/collective care support.
The Funds further made concerted outreach efforts, for example, to better reach and understand the needs of women with disabilities and groups responding to the climate crisis, to expand their advisor networks, and to sharpen their analyses of the contexts defenders are working in, particularly in situations of displacement and harder to reach geographies. The Urgent Action Funds also took steps to strengthen grantmaking systems/platforms for increased accessibility and inclusivity (format, language) and integrity.
Objective 3)
Each Urgent Action Fund provided grants and accompaniment to support defenders to bolster their ability to sustain their work and strengthen their resilience. 55% of the overall grantmaking supported collective care for HRDs and groups. These grants supported spaces for care, reflection, and peer learning, for example, through convening regional advisors or bringing together grantee partners facing shared issues across countries. Support for crisis preparedness helped grantee partners promote participation and inclusion so their communities are better equipped and empowered to respond to climate-related disasters or social crises, and so that systems and practices are more responsive to marginalized groups. The Urgent Action Funds also supported collective care actions that built connections and enhanced solidarity, such as responding to the needs of displaced communities through aid.
Grantee responses to conflict-affected communities have according to UAF demonstrated how collective care during crisis response can support immediate survival, safety and protection, solidarity and connection. Across various countries, grantees provided humanitarian aid support infrastructure; created shared resources and networks to raise awareness and affirm refugees rights in a different country; and engaged and mobilized community members to advocate for their rights to access services and programs.
Objective 4)
The Urgent Action Funds are members of a core group of twelve feminist funds (African Womens Development Fund, Dalan Fund, Equality Fund, Global Fund for Women, MADRE Purposeful / Global Resilience Fund, Ukrainian Womens Fund, all four Urgent Action Funds, and Womens Fund Asia) that have been collaborating to set up the First Response Fund, a new global humanitarian pooled fund offering donors the opportunity to narrow the funding gap and leverage the unique strengths of Women-Led Organizations(WLOs)/Women Rights Organizations (WROs) in crisis response. The Funds central innovation is leveraging the existing network of national, regional and multiregional Womens and Feminist Funds (W/FF) who work in partnership with WROs and WLOs before, during, and after humanitarian crises.
